messages.subject: Re: irace issue with parallel cores
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dr. López-Ibáñez,

I'm facing the same problem, but my error message it's a little bit different:

================================================================
Erro: == irace == The output of targetRunner must be one number 'cost'!

== irace == The call to targetRunner was:

/home/klevison/Downloads/iRace/tuning-green/target-runner 1 1 1263080864 /home/klevison/Downloads/iRace/tuning-green/instances/Data_N=6_M=3_T=10times5.dat   --MAX_ILS 500 --MAX_TENT 3

== irace == The output was:

0.354955
== irace == This is not a bug in irace, but means that something failed when running the command(s) above or they were terminated before completion. Try to run the command(s) above from the execution directory '/home/klevison/Downloads/iRace/tuning-green' to investigate the issue.
Execução interrompida
================================================================

I'm new in irace, so at first, I was forgetting to print the cost in my executable, but one colleague told me to do it to correct this, but the error persists
even that the cost had been printed and the correct value was found, once that this number (0.354955) is the optimal value for this problem in this instance.

Can you help me with that?

Thank you in advance!

Best Regards,

Klevison Ribeiro

Em segunda-feira, 31 de outubro de 2016 11:57:09 UTC-2, Manuel López-Ibáñez escreveu:
> On Monday, 31 October 2016 11:31:44 UTC, Mohamed El Yafrani wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I'm having a hard time running EDA in parallel on a university server. When I tried to use 10, 16, and 3 cores (by setting parallel to N in scenario.txt), I got the following error (repeated several times):
> >
> > Any ideas how to solve this issue ?
>
> Dear Mohamed,
>
> There may be a bug in irace, but usually when one gets the above error, there is some problem in target-runner. A few things worth checking:
>
> * Does 'only one core' mean that you run with parallel=1 on the same machine that gives the error with parallel=2? The key here is 'on the same machine'. If you need to submit jobs through a queuing system, the running environment when using the queuing system may not be the same as when you launch irace yourself. The queuing system may also send the job to different machines depending on the number of CPUs requested.
>
> * Does target-runner read/create intermediate files? Can these files cause a race condition when two calls to target-runner happen at the same time? Maybe these files consume too much memory or fill the filesystem when there are simultaneous target-runner calls?
>
> * Does your university server impose any limits on number of processes, CPU/memory/filesystem use per job? Such limits may kill the target-runner process before it has a chance to print anything useful and irace cannot detect what the problem is.
>
> You could try to create a dummy target-runner that only prints what you expect to be printed by the actual target-runner without executing any other program or reading/writing any files, and see if that works.
>
> Manuel.

Este e-mail foi enviado por um ALUNO da Universidade Federal de Ouro Preto e não reflete a posição da Instituição.

messages.subject: Re: irace issue with parallel cores
messages.body_plain:
Dear Klevison,

I wonder if this may be due to the language settings of your operating system versus the language of the numbers printed. I'd suggest to change the system  locale to English.

Another possibility is that the output contains some unprintable characters that prevent parsing it as a number. Save the output of target-runner to a file and examine it with an editor that can show non-printable characters, such as Emacs.

If nothing else works, please send us your scenario file and target-runner.

Cheers,

Manuel

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

One friend here in the university send me another target-runner that did work and was possible to run irace with it. I did not understand very well, but she told me that this new target-runner treats more than one output of the program. I did not understand why this was the problem, because my program was printing one number cost only, I did test and confirm this running de program outside of irace. So, it seems that this was the problem, but now it's working very well.

I'm sending the two target-runners, the old and the new one that works, in case you have a curiosity to know what happened. But the only difference between them it's the lines 52 and 58.

Link to target-runners: https://www.dropbox.com/sh/lb2lpjld5nu54o4/AAAHIbNHnyymEAGRFDMBUsvha?dl=0

Thanks for the help and best regards!

Klevison Ribeiro

messages.subject: Re: irace issue with parallel cores
messages.body_plain:
Comparing the two, in the old target-runner, your EXE supposedly prints the number. In this new target-runner, the target-runner itself parses the number and prints it. My guess is that your EXE is printing other (invisible) things besides the number, so irace cannot process the output, but the new target-runner removes those invisible things.
